questions.stem: Why do rising greenhouse gas levels worry biologists?

options.text: Because more trapped heat raises the average temperature of the Earth
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Because the gases poison plants directly
options.explanation: The concern is heat trapping, not direct poisoning.

questions.stem: State what a greenhouse gas does.
questions.modelAnswer: A greenhouse gas absorbs infrared radiation so heat remains trapped in the atmosphere of the Earth.

questions.stem: Name the gas released by cattle as they digest grass.
questions.modelAnswer: Methane is released by cattle as they digest grass.

questions.stem: Explain why CFCs concern environmental scientists despite low volumes.
questions.modelAnswer: CFCs concern scientists because they are potent greenhouse gases among the named set, so even small releases add to trapped heat.

questions.stem: A nation cuts fossil fuel use but expands rice paddies. Predict its gas profile.
questions.modelAnswer: Carbon dioxide emissions fall, but methane emissions rise as the paddy fields release more methane, so its greenhouse profile shifts between the two gases.
